office_does: One of the 2nd District's two members of the Washington House, voting on state law and the state budgets for a two-year term.
race_blurb: First-term Republican Matt Marshall, a former Eatonville school director and Army veteran, faces Democrat Angela Taylor, a Yelm small-business owner in her first race. Marshall runs against new taxes and on parents' authority; Taylor on school funding, rural healthcare and limits on health-industry money.

candidates.summary: First-term representative, former Eatonville school director, Army veteran and physician assistant, running against new taxes and the income tax and for parents' authority.
highlights: Pledges to oppose new taxes and fight the income tax; voted against ESSB 6346 [S1][S3]
Voted against the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S7][S8]
Offered amendments to let parents inspect school-held medical and counseling records [S11][S12]
Opposes a mega airport in the area and supports an elected sheriff [S1]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet pledge to oppose new taxes and the income tax, plus nay votes on ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5814.

spending.basis: Running to stop 'out of control government spending' and cut fees, regulations and hidden costs.

experience.basis: First-term incumbent and former school director, against a candidate with no elected experience.

local-control.basis: Opposes siting any mega airport in the area and defends keeping an elected sheriff.

parental-rights.basis: Pledges to defend parents' authority, voted against ESHB 1296, and sought parental access to school-held health and counseling records.

candidates.summary: Yelm small-business owner and caregiver in her first race, running on fully funded schools, rural healthcare access and a fairer tax system.
highlights: Wants to correct a 'regressive tax system' and direct new revenue to property-tax relief [S2]
Pledges not to take contributions over $200 from health-industry executives, lobbyists or PACs [S2]
Calls for fully funded Pre-K-12 schools and a centralized rural hospital [S1][S2]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S3][S4]

taxes.basis: Wants to correct a regressive tax system and redirect new revenue to property-tax relief, while also seeking B&O relief for small businesses.

spending.basis: Calls for fully funded Pre-K-12 education and a rural hospital, alongside 'responsible budgets'.

safety.basis: Would support legislation that expands resources for law enforcement and sheriff collaboration.

reform.basis: Pledges to cap contributions from health-industry interests and criticizes corporate and insurance influence in Olympia.

healthcare.basis: Says she will 'fight for healthcare for all' and criticizes a profit-driven system, without naming a mechanism.

experience.basis: No elected experience, running against an incumbent.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no stated position.
